svg.title: ESP32-S3 hardware and cloud inference architecture
svg.desc: Two separate ESP32-S3 boards provide direct LAN preview and camera capture. The camera uploads JPEGs with a bearer token over Wi-Fi and HTTPS. Dashboard saves frames into event storage. worker.py checks each complete event with YOLO. All false detections discard photos as normal and skip Qwen. Any positive detection sends all ordered frames to Qwen-LoRA for a verdict and evidence. Policy stores a device-facing result. The camera polls via HTTPS for up to 60 seconds and alarms only on suspicious; normal, review, exempted and timeout do not trigger an alarm. Optional family exemption is disabled by default. Incomplete events and inference errors retain evidence for review. In normal mode, PIR warms for 30 seconds and arms after an inactive LOW reading. Motion HIGH requests a burst. The request waits for pending uploads, AI polling and camera ownership to clear, expires after 10 seconds if not accepted, and captures up to five JPEGs when accepted. Rearming requires LOW and the 10-second cooldown after the previous capture. Hardware photographs show a Waveshare touch LCD and an ESP32-S3-EYE reference board; the actual camera board remains unconfirmed. The Qwen node includes its official logo. Hardware nodes have explicit connection ports. A single hollow double-headed LAN arrow represents authenticated control and live preview. A dorm-room cartoon is only an example of uploaded frames, not an inference result. The camera maps suspicious to its alarm outputs; pending responses continue polling.

svg.metadata: Current local implementation at c5e98e5511725217575cf92591149a0c7affcc72. Image and alarm flow; audio and enrollment omitted. Sources: firmware/camera/main/project_event_upload.cpp:59-108; firmware/camera/main/project_ai_alarm.cpp:54-139; firmware/camera/main/project_settings.h:8-9,23,43; server/worker.py:8-48,62-90,102-180; server/event_queue.py:195-265; server/device_alarm_api.py:28-51; server/alarm_policy.py:9-76. PIR logic: firmware/camera/main/project_sensors.cpp:114-162,265-292; firmware/camera/main/project_settings.h:14-43; firmware/camera/main/project_core.h:20. Normal mode shown. Embedded assets: LCD photograph — https://www.waveshare.com/media/catalog/product/cache/1/image/800x800/9df78eab33525d08d6e5fb8d27136e95/e/s/esp32-s3-touch-lcd-2.8-2.jpg (Waveshare product page); camera reference photograph — https://www.espressif.com/sites/all/themes/espressif/images/esp-eye/esp-s3-eye.png (Espressif ESP32-S3-EYE product page); Qwen logo — https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i4/O1CN01OXv3EM1FN8t9W4P79_!!6000000000474-2-tps-80-80.png (qwen.ai favicon). Hardware photographs are illustrative and do not establish physical board compatibility. Visual update: Times New Roman bold headings with SimSun Chinese serif fallback, explicit same-LAN preview, hardware connection ports, status-specific device responses, inline native SVG pictograms, and an illustrative dorm-frame thumbnail. The cartoon is an input example, not a confirmed detection. Only suspicious activates the physical alarm; pending responses keep polling. Typography and spacing update: all labels inherit one bold serif family; headings 32 px, body and annotations 24 px. Arrow strokes are 3.2 px. Enlarged alarm symbols have separate text clearances. The dorm image is a side illustration beside the straight camera-to-Upload-API arrow. PowerPoint-oriented font explicitness: each text and tspan stores its final font-family, font-size in px, font-weight 700, font-style normal, and fill as SVG presentation attributes. Class-based text CSS has been removed. Text remains live SVG text; font files are not embedded. PowerPoint conversion has not been verified. Connection simplification: one hollow bidirectional LAN arrow with a Wi-Fi icon; suspicious-image illustration beside the upload arrow; Result API relocated to the upper-right cloud extension. HTTPS polling uses one orthogonal bend. Report state and normal/no-person state feed a shared rail; the curved crossover at x=1320 denotes no connection to the YOLO deletion path.
